newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-JUNINHO GETS FIRST FEEL OF VICENTE CALDERON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUNINHO GETS FIRST FEEL OF VICENTE CALDERON.

text.p: Brazilian midfielder Juninho laced up his football boots and got his first feel of the pitch at Atletico Madrid's Vicente Calderon stadium on Thursday.
"It feels goods," said the $20.2 million signing from English club Middlesbrough.
It was a promising start. After all, the stadium will be his home for the next five years.
Hardly anyone was at Madrid's Barajas Airport to greet the 24-year-old on Wednesday.

Perhaps because after two months of speculation in the Spanish media about whether he would be coming to the roji blancos -- the red and whites -- as Atletico are known locally, no one could believe he was finally going to arrive.
However when he was formally presented to the fans and media, the reception could not have been more different.
More than a thousand members of Atletico supporters' club turned out to celebrate the arrival of the club's new star attraction.
A huge cheer echoed around the ground when Juninho walked out in full club strip and raised a club scarf above his heard.
There is little doubt Atletico fans have already taken Juninho to their hearts in a similar fashion to the way Middlesbrough supporters adored him.
Equally clear is that there will not be much discussion with manager Radomir Antic about the role he will play on the pitch.
"I will play the same way I did in Brazil and in England," said Juninho.
"I hope to be given free rein around the pitch."
One thing Antic will have to do is give Juninho some protection from the notoriously brutal tackling in Spanish league football.
At just 1.67 metres tall he is one of the smallest players in the league.
"I expect the tackling to be hard but I hope players will be fair," he said.
An English football magazine recently said that Juninho completed 69 per cent of his 271 attempts to dribble balls past opponents last season.
